clue.text: One possibly struggling on line, having zero memory over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the whole assembly is turned so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: zero is nil
RAM is computer memory (random-access memory)

explanation.surface: A tired person struggles on, having forgotten everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns NILRAM round. The definition is cryptic: a game fish hooked on an angler's line fights it.
explanation.definitionFit: A big game fish famous for the long fight it gives an angler once hooked on the line.

clue.text: Rodgers and Hammerstein's last Illinois performance. The end

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the lyricist Hammerstein's name

parts.note: IL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Illinois

indicators.note: The end, after the full stop, asks for the final letter of the word performance

explanation.surface: Reads like a programme note on the last show of a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical in Illinois.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rodgers and Hammerstein' looks like one unit, but the definition is Rodgers alone: Nile Rodgers of the disco band Chic. 'The end' takes the eleventh and final letter of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile Rodgers is the American guitarist and producer who co-founded Chic; his first name defines the answer.

clue.text: 21 detailed in error

indicators.note: detailed means each of the pair has its tail, its final letter, cut off

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is a slang plural for breasts, so a pair of boobs, BOOB and BOOB

explanation.surface: A cheeky cross-reference: the 21 across item has been shown in detail by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to TITS, read as a pair of BOOBs; 'detailed' docks the last B of each, leaving BOO and BOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is an informal word for a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Billions invested in its flotation; net asset value unknown

parts.note: NAV is the standard financial abbreviation for net asset value
an unknown in algebra is x, y or z; here Y

explanation.surface: A financial report on a stock market flotation, with billions invested and the company's value not yet known.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'flotation' is not a share issue but keeping warships afloat, which costs billions.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's sea force costs billions of public money to keep its ships afloat, a cryptic description.

clue.text: British university lecturer takes a friend out to go for a stroll

indicators.note: takes means the pair named after it are taken around the first three letters
out says the words a friend sit on the outside of those letters

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A British academic takes a friend out for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'out' put the friend round the abbreviations, which go in after its first two letters rather than at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulate is a formal verb meaning to walk about, the same as strolling.

clue.text: Wicked outsiders evicted from Mount of Olives

indicators.note: Mount, in a down clue, means the letters rise, so they read upwards
the outer letters of Olives are thrown out, leaving its inside

explanation.surface: A wicked eviction of outsiders from the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsiders evicted from' leaves LIVE; 'Mount' turns it upward. 'Mount of Olives' looks like a fixed place name, but Mount is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil and wicked are synonymous adjectives for morally bad.

clue.text: Some superstar comedian turned politician

indicators.note: turned says the letters taken run backwards
Some means only a part of the words superstar comedian is taken

explanation.surface: A famous comic turned politician, as some celebrities do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes TARCOMED from superstar comedian and 'turned' reverses it. 'turned politician' reads like a career change.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is a political figure, a politician by example.

clue.text: Cabot in America, travelling west over prairie land

indicators.note: travelling west says the hidden letters are read backwards
over says the answer's letters stretch over the words Cabot in America, spanning the gaps between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The explorer John Cabot in the New World, heading westward across the prairies.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'over prairie land' is changed: 'over' does not define a province, it signals letters spread over Cabot in America. In an across clue 'travelling west' reads them right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian province lying largely on the great grassland plains of the interior.

clue.text: Some trafficked imported sex films

indicators.note: imported says something is brought inside the rearranged letters
trafficked suggests goods moved about illegally, so the letters of Some are rearranged

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Some of the films seized were illegally imported pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trafficked' rearranges the first word; 'imported' brings the numeral inside. 'sex' looks English but is the Latin for six.
explanation.definitionFit: Movies is the everyday name for films shown in cinemas.

clue.text: Complete rejection of EU; pound down

indicators.note: complete rejection turns the whole of what follows back on itself, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A Brexit headline: Britain rejects the EU outright and sterling falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound down' reads as a falling currency, but pound is the weight LB and down is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and feeling down both mean being sad or low in spirits.

clue.text: A buoy adrift in southern backwater

indicators.note: a buoy adrift has broken loose and wanders, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A buoy has broken its mooring and floats loose in a southern creek.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshy, slow-moving creek or backwater found in the southern United States, especially Louisiana.

clue.text: Simpleton left naked?

parts.note: someone naked has nothing on, read as O (nothing) and ON

explanation.surface: A fool is left standing without clothes, like the emperor in the fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'naked' is split into 'nothing on', giving O for nothing plus ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A loon is an informal word for a foolish or crazy person, a synonym of simpleton.

clue.text: As one might address Speedy Gonzales, endlessly huge

indicators.note: endlessly means both ends are cut off the phrase

parts.words: As one might address Speedy Gonzales
parts.note: Speedy Gonzales is the Mexican cartoon mouse, so one might address him in Spanish as Señor Mouse

explanation.surface: A chatty aside about how you might greet the cartoon mouse Speedy Gonzales.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedy Gonzales is the fast Mexican mouse of Warner Bros cartoons, so you might hail him 'Señor Mouse'; 'endlessly' drops the S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and huge are synonyms for very large.

clue.text: Get out of bed about noon to wash

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to get out of bed is to rise

explanation.surface: A lie-in until about midday, then up for a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it in clean water.

clue.text: Special instrument's raised pitch

parts.note: a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A particular instrument has been tuned up to a higher pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a note that is sharp is pitched a semitone higher, or slightly too high.

clue.text: Hope to see Piraeus playing United away

indicators.note: playing suggests the remaining letters are in motion and rearranged
away says the letter for United is taken out of Piraeus

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A football fan hopes to watch the Piraeus side play a United team away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Piraeus is the port of Athens, home of Olympiacos. 'away' removes U, leaving PIRAES, and 'playing' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something, a synonymous verb.

clue.text: Safe, principled chap

definitions.meaning: old criminal slang for a safe, as in a safe-cracker called a peterman
the ... Principle, that people rise to their level of incompetence, is named after Laurence J. ...

explanation.surface: A dependable man of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is thieves' slang for a strongbox, and Laurence Peter gave his name to a principle.

clue.text: Low note made by one who jumped over it?

definitions.text: Low note made by one who jumped over it?

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: A riddle about the nursery rhyme cow and the sound it made.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Hey Diddle Diddle' the cow jumped over the moon; its low is MOO. The whole clue also points to the thing it jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the cow jumped over the satellite of Earth, so it is what she leapt.

clue.text: Known for its snakebite, I'd popped into old pub The Scotsman

indicators.note: popped into says the letters I'd are slipped inside the rest

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, so a crossword Scotsman
the clue's I'd supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman drops into an old pub famous for its snakebite, the lager and cider drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakebite is a British pub drink of lager and cider; here the 'snakebite' is a snake's literal bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means relating to snakes, the reptiles whose bite is known and feared.

clue.text: A blubbery character, Henry gets stuck into whiskey and beer

indicators.note: gets stuck into means one letter is pushed inside the others

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ale is a kind of beer
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A tearful, blubbering Henry tucks into whiskey and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubbery' suggests someone weeping, but it is about blubber, the fat of a sea mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea mammal insulated by a thick layer of fat called blubber.

clue.text: One grapples with the remnants of the French Resistance

parts.note: the rest is what remains
le is French for the
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A survivor of the wartime French Resistance still grapples with its legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Resistance' reads as the wartime movement, but the words split: LE for 'the French', R for resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a fighter who grapples with an opponent.

clue.text: Little peckers regular features of strip-tease, I'm told!

definitions.meaning: small songbirds such as the blue and great varieties, which peck for food

definitions.text: regular features of strip-tease, I'm told!
definitions.meaning: a slang word for breasts, routinely on show in a strip act

explanation.surface: A smutty aside about small birds and what a strip show displays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a family of small birds and coarse slang for women's breasts.

clue.text: It's said to elicit a smile from one about to be shot

definitions.text: It's said to elicit a smile from one about to be shot

parts.words: It's said to elicit a smile from one about to be shot
parts.note: photographers ask their subjects to say this word, which shapes the mouth into a smile; shot means photographed

explanation.surface: A grim scene of someone smiling before a firing squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests an execution, but it means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers tell people to say this dairy word because saying it pulls the mouth into a grin.

clue.text: Blairite organisation's spin doctor; fearful woman

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the trade of a spin doctor
an ogress is a frightening female monster

explanation.surface: A Blairite group's spin doctor is described as a terrifying woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress was a pressure group within the Labour Party that promoted Tony Blair's New Labour politics.

clue.text: End of fairytale story upset one in bed

indicators.note: upset says these letters are knocked over and rearranged
End of picks the final letter of fairytale

explanation.surface: A child in bed is upset by how a bedtime fairy story ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in bed' suggests a sleeper, but the bed is an oyster bed on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are farmed and found in groups on the seabed called beds.

clue.text: Pirate remix of Elvis (the King)

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters of Elvis are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A pirated remix of a track by Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll.
explanation.walkthrough: '(the King)' looks like Elvis's nickname, but it gives R. 'Pirate' suggests bootleg music; it is a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island.

clue.text: Rework script of Spielberg classic to include tragic princess

indicators.note: to include means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film
Di is Diana, Princess of Wales, who died in a car crash in 1997

explanation.surface: A plan to rewrite E.T. with Princess Diana added to the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or rework a piece of writing.

clue.text: Torture occasionally gets the right answer

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters of torture are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: A grim claim that torture sometimes extracts the correct answer.
explanation.definitionFit: True and right are synonyms when said of a correct answer.

clue.text: Dregs of bitter in barrels goes sour

indicators.note: in places the final letter of bitter inside the other word

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for beer or wine

indicators.note: dregs are what is left at the bottom, so the last letter of bitter

explanation.surface: Bitter beer left at the bottom of the barrels has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that turns has curdled, gone sour.

clue.text: Without a question Thérèse, that's a helluva bust!

indicators.note: Without says the letters that follow are removed from the surname

parts.note: Thérèse Raquin is the title heroine of Émile Zola's novel

explanation.surface: An exclamation about Thérèse's magnificent bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' suggests a bosom, but means financial collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is total collapse or bankruptcy, a really big bust.

clue.text: Corbyn's first (and last) description of his political movement?

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of Corbyn

parts.note: ult., ultimo, is the abbreviation for last month

explanation.surface: Jeremy Corbyn, Labour leader, names his political movement for the first and last time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a jibe: critics called Corbyn's Momentum movement a personality-driven sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Detractors described the devoted following around Corbyn as a sect built around one leader.

clue.text: Taxi driver finally accepted fare in shell suit

indicators.note: accepted means the taxi takes that letter inside it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of driver

explanation.surface: A taxi driver finally takes a passenger wearing a shell suit, the shiny nylon tracksuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a passenger, but means food; a 'shell suit' is the 1980s nylon tracksuit, here a crustacean's shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A crustacean eaten as seafood, served with its body encased in a hard shell.

clue.text: Amateurish painting featuring Northern European river

indicators.note: featuring means the daub contains the next letter

parts.note: a daub is a crude, unskilled painting

explanation.surface: An amateur painting of a river in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major river flowing through central and eastern Europe.

clue.text: Repeated it time and time again: education

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone stressed education over and over, like a slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes Tony Blair's slogan 'Education, education, education'.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, so iterated means repeated.
